q: The Lapidus-Pang-Man result on wave maps and the Klainerman null condition: nonlinear wave equations □u = N(u,∂u) have global small-data solutions when N satisfies the null condition. The null condition means:
opts: N(u,∂u) contains only products of derivatives with a factor that vanishes on the light cone (null cone)
exp: Klainerman's null condition: the nonlinearity N involves contractions of derivatives with respect to the Minkowski metric that vanish on the null cone |ξ| = |τ| in Fourier space. This prevents resonant interactions on the light cone and allows global existence for small data, crucial for the stability of Minkowski space.
